text: Categorical conjugation becomes exactly the coordinate algebra map for (g,x)↦gxg⁻¹, with the first tensor factor conjugating the second. The proof compares generalized points and their convolution products, matching [Milne, inner automorphisms](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=43). Reversing the opposite-category arrow produces an algebra map H→H⊗H; it does not claim joint conjugation is a group homomorphism. Checks pass: [productMap_comp_conjugationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Conjugation.lean#L101), [grpObjPointsMulEquiv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Yoneda.lean#L338).
The coordinate map evaluates to the expected conjugate.
Generalized points have their original algebra homomorphisms.

This is the coordinate map of left conjugation: multiply the first universal point, the second, and the inverse of the first by convolution. Evaluating gives gxg⁻¹, the orientation of [Milne, inner automorphisms](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=43). Commutativity of the coordinate semiring makes the tensor square a valid value algebra; the represented group itself need not be abelian. Checks pass: [productMap_comp_conjugationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Conjugation.lean#L101), [conjugationAlgHom_counit_left](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Conjugation.lean#L172), [conjugationAlgHom_coassoc](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Conjugation.lean#L243).
Arbitrary algebra-valued points evaluate to gxg⁻¹.
The identity acts trivially.
Successive conjugations satisfy the left-action law.

The conjugation coordinate map, viewed as a universal point, is i₁*i₂*i₁⁻¹, where i₁(a)=a⊗1 and i₂(a)=1⊗a. This exposes the gxg⁻¹ order of [Milne, inner automorphisms](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=43). The multiplication is convolution from the coproduct, not pointwise multiplication of coordinate functions; tensor-factor maps are not being asserted injective. Checks pass: [productMap_comp_conjugationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Conjugation.lean#L101), [conjugationAlgHom_counit_right](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Conjugation.lean#L192).
Evaluation retains the first-variable conjugation order.
Conjugating the identity returns the identity point.

Any algebra map φ:H⊗H→A evaluates conjugation by conjugating its second restriction with its first. Postcomposition preserves convolution products and inverses, so the universal formula gives this equality directly, in the convention of [Milne, inner automorphisms](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=43). The value semiring A is commutative; φ is only an algebra map, not a Hopf morphism. Checks pass: [productMap_comp_conjugationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Conjugation.lean#L101), [productMap_one_id_comp_conjugationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Conjugation.lean#L149).
The tensor product map of two points gives their group-theoretic conjugate.
Setting the first point to the identity gives the identity map.

Evaluating a pure tensor by a⊗b↦g(a)x(b) turns the conjugation coordinate map into the point gxg⁻¹. This verifies both tensor-factor order and inverse placement against [Milne, inner automorphisms](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=43). The inverse belongs to the convolution group of algebra-valued points, so it is defined for every g without any pointwise nonzero-value condition. Checks pass: [productMap_one_id_comp_conjugationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Conjugation.lean#L149), [productMap_id_one_comp_conjugationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Conjugation.lean#L161).
The identity conjugator acts trivially.
Conjugation fixes the identity point.

A bialgebra map between commutative Hopf algebras intertwines their conjugation coordinate maps: applying it to both tensor factors agrees with applying it before conjugation. On points this is preservation of gxg⁻¹, as in [Milne, inner automorphisms](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=43). The bialgebra hypothesis supplies coproduct and counit preservation; inverse preservation then follows automatically for the induced group map. Checks pass: [comp_conjugationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Conjugation.lean#L85), [productMap_comp_conjugationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Conjugation.lean#L101).
Postcomposition computes conjugation through the two restrictions.
Point evaluation fixes the intended conjugation order.

For a base-valued point g, this sends a coordinate function f to T_gf, where (T_gf)(x)=f(xg), exactly [Milne, right regular representation](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=98). Algebraically it contracts the second coproduct factor with g. It is an algebra endomorphism over any commutative base ring; translation generally does not preserve the group identity and is not asserted to be a Hopf morphism. Checks pass: [rightTranslationAlgHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L66), [toConv_comp_rightTranslationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L77).
The coproduct contraction uses the second factor.
Evaluating at x gives the product point xg.

Translation replaces a coordinate a with ∑a₁g(a₂), contracting the second coproduct factor and identifying H⊗k with H. This is the coordinate formula for [Milne, right regular representation](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=98). The displayed tensor map avoids choosing a particular sum of pure tensors; its value is independent of how the coproduct is written. Checks pass: [rightTranslationAlgEquiv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L256), [ofConv_rightTranslationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L90).
The automorphism has the same tensor-contraction formula.
Applying a point evaluates the convolution product in the correct order.

If f and g are base-valued points, evaluating coordinates after translation by g produces their convolution product f*g. Thus the represented point moves from f to fg, matching [Milne, right regular representation](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=98). The equality is of complete algebra-valued points and follows from the coproduct formula, without assuming rational points determine every coordinate function. Checks pass: [ofConv_rightTranslationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L90), [counitAlgHom_comp_rightTranslationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L268).
The equation holds on every coordinate.
At the identity point it specializes to g.

For each coordinate a, evaluating its translate at f gives (f*g)(a). This is the elementwise version of (T_ga)(f)=a(fg) in [Milne, right regular representation](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=98). Here f and g are points, whereas a is a coordinate function; the product on points is convolution, and no multiplication or composition of the functions f and g is substituted. Checks pass: [toConv_comp_rightTranslationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L77), [counitAlgHom_comp_rightTranslationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L268).
The complete point equality yields this evaluation.
Identity-point evaluation recovers the translating point.

Right translation is an algebra automorphism: its inverse is translation by the inverse point, as expected from [Milne, §1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=20). The construction obtains bijectivity from the regular-comodule point action and retains the stated coordinate map. It requires a commutative Hopf algebra over a commutative ring, with no field, finite-type or reducedness assumption. Checks pass: [rightTranslationAlgEquiv_toAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L133), [rightTranslationAlgEquiv_inv](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L231).
The automorphism retains the translation algebra map.
Translation by g⁻¹ is the inverse automorphism.

The automorphism’s underlying algebra homomorphism is the original right-translation pullback, with the convention of [Milne, right regular representation](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=98). Bijectivity has been proved for that function and then packaged as an equivalence. Forgetting the inverse data therefore leaves every coordinate value unchanged; this does not merely identify two abstractly isomorphic coordinate algebras. Checks pass: [rightTranslationAlgEquiv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L256), [toConv_rightTranslationAlgEquiv](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L140).
The equivalence evaluates by the original coproduct formula.
Its universal-point description is unchanged.

The coordinate automorphism is the convolution product of the universal point id_H and the constant H-valued point obtained from g:k-valued. This is precisely the right-regular convention of [Milne, right regular representation](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=98). Extending g through k→H supplies the constant second factor; no coordinate-function inverse or assumption that g takes only unit values occurs. Checks pass: [rightTranslationAlgEquiv_toAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L133), [toConv_comp_rightTranslationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L77).
The packaged map is the specified translation map.
Evaluation gives right multiplication by g.

Translation by the identity point is the identity algebra automorphism, the unit law of [Milne, right regular representation](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=98). The point denoted 1 is the counit, while 1 on the automorphism side means the identity function. The regular-comodule counit law proves the equality, so it holds over arbitrary commutative base rings. Checks pass: [rightTranslationAlgHom_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L206), [rightTranslationAlgEquiv_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L183).
Forgetting the equivalence gives the identity algebra map.
The compatible multiplication law also holds.

The pullbacks satisfy T_(gh)=T_g∘T_h, as in [Milne, right regular representation](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=98): applying them to f at x gives f((xg)h). Multiplication of algebra automorphisms means function composition, with T_h applied first to the function. This agrees with contravariant pullback of right translations and requires no commutativity of the point group. Checks pass: [rightTranslationAlgHom_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L213), [rightTranslationAlgEquiv_inv](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L231).
The underlying algebra maps have the same composition order.
Inverse points give inverse automorphisms.

The identity point induces the identity coordinate endomorphism, specializing the right-regular action of [Milne, right regular representation](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=98). The point’s 1 is its counit map, rather than the constant function with value 1. Contracting that counit with the coproduct recovers each coordinate, and forgetting the automorphism wrapper preserves this unit law. Checks pass: [rightTranslationAlgEquiv_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L169), [rightTranslationAlgHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L66).
The stronger automorphism-level unit identity holds.
Coproduct contraction gives the underlying coordinate action.

Translation by g*h has coordinate map T_g∘T_h. This is the same right-regular action order as [Milne, right regular representation](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=98), because functions pull back contravariantly: (T_g(T_hf))(x)=f((xg)h). The star on points is convolution, while comp on algebra maps is ordinary composition; confusing those operations would reverse the intended calculation. Checks pass: [rightTranslationAlgEquiv_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L183), [toConv_comp_rightTranslationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L77).
The automorphisms satisfy the same law.
Evaluating translation acts by right multiplication on points.

This is the subgroup of base-valued points whose right translation fixes one specified coordinate function, under [Milne, right regular representation](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=98). Identity, products and inverses preserve that equality by the action laws. It records an ordinary subgroup of G(k); it does not construct a scheme-theoretic stabilizer or claim such a stabilizer is smooth. Checks pass: [mem_rightTranslationStabilizer](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L250), [rightTranslationAlgHom_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L213), [rightTranslationAlgEquiv_inv](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L231).
Membership is exactly equality of the translated coordinate function.
The action composition supplies product closure.
The inverse action supplies inverse closure.

A point belongs to this stabilizer exactly when T_gf=f as elements of the coordinate algebra. This is literal function invariance for [Milne, right regular representation](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=98), not merely agreement on all base-valued points. That distinction avoids assuming point density or reducedness; the declaration concerns the ordinary point subgroup and makes no scheme-representability assertion. Checks pass: [rightTranslationAlgHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L66), [rightTranslationAlgHom_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L213).
The equality uses the actual coproduct contraction.
The defining equality is preserved by the action product.

Evaluating a translated coordinate at the identity gives its value at g: ε∘T_g=g. This is (T_gf)(e)=f(eg)=f(g), consistent with [Milne, right regular representation](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=98). The proof uses the counit as the convolution identity, over an arbitrary commutative base ring; it does not require kernels to be prime ideals. Checks pass: [toConv_comp_rightTranslationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L77), [comap_rightTranslationAlgEquiv_augmentationPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L328).
The general point-evaluation identity specializes to the counit.
Over a field the augmentation spectrum point translates to g.

Translation pulls ker ε back to ker g. [Mathlib’s height invariance](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Height.lean#L306) proves their heights equal, using the prime-chain notion of [Stacks, prime height](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00KD). Here general ideal height is the infimum over minimal primes in ℕ∪{∞}; over a general base ring neither kernel is assumed prime, nor the height finite. Checks pass: [counitAlgHom_comp_rightTranslationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L268).
The translated counit identifies the two kernels.

Right translation induces a homeomorphism of the entire prime spectrum, agreeing with the translation-isomorphism principle of [Milne, §1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=20). Its map is contraction along T_g. The inverse algebra equivalence appears in the constructor because that constructor itself contracts along an inverse; this double reversal gives right translation, not translation by g⁻¹. Checks pass: [rightTranslationHomeomorph_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L311), [comap_rightTranslationAlgEquiv_augmentationPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L328).
The forward map is explicitly contraction along T_g.
Over a field it sends the identity point to g.

The spectrum homeomorphism sends a prime ideal p to T_g⁻¹(p), its inverse image under the coordinate automorphism. This is the contravariant spectrum action corresponding to translation in [Milne, §1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=20). The inverse-image notation denotes contraction of an ideal, not evaluation of the inverse function on each element, and applies to every prime of H. Checks pass: [rightTranslationAlgEquiv_inv](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L231), [comap_rightTranslationAlgEquiv_augmentationPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L328).
The inverse point supplies the inverse automorphism.
The augmentation-point computation confirms the forward direction.

Over a field, contracting the augmentation ideal along T_g gives ker g, so the identity spectrum point is translated to g, as in [Milne, §1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=20). The field hypothesis makes these kernels actual prime points. The proof is the equation ε∘T_g=g, not an assumption that every spectrum point is rational. Checks pass: [counitAlgHom_comp_rightTranslationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L268), [rightTranslationHomeomorph_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L311).
The coordinate counit composition is g.
The homeomorphism uses this contraction direction.

A coordinate Hopf morphism intertwines translation by a point with translation by its image: F(xg)=F(x)F(g). The displayed algebra maps run in the reverse direction, consistent with [Milne, right regular representation](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=98). The translating point belongs to the target coordinate algebra’s base-valued points and is pulled back along the bialgebra morphism; no injectivity is assumed. Checks pass: [toConv_comp_rightTranslationAlgHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L77), [rightTranslationAlgHom_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Translation.lean#L213).
Translation on points is right multiplication.
The coordinate action has the expected composition law.

Semilinear maps with a fixed scalar homomorphism form a module under pointwise scalar multiplication in the target. The extra scalar action must commute with the target’s original scalar action; otherwise scaling a map need not preserve semilinearity. The acting semiring need not be commutative, and additive inverses are not required. Compared with [Schweigert Thm.1.1.5](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L948).

Maps semilinear for the same scalar homomorphism form a commutative additive monoid: add their values pointwise, and use the zero map as identity. The modules may be over semirings and need not admit subtraction. Fixing the scalar homomorphism matters; maps with unrelated scalar rules are not being added here. Compared with [Schweigert Thm.1.1.5](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L845).

When the target has additive inverses, semilinear maps with a fixed scalar homomorphism form an abelian group under pointwise addition. Negation and subtraction are computed in the target. The source only needs a commutative additive monoid, so this construction does not require subtraction in the source or scalar rings. Compared with [Schweigert Thm.1.1.5](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L889).

Composition applies g first and then f. For semilinear maps, their scalar homomorphisms compose in the same order: a scalar first passes through g’s homomorphism and then f’s. The stated compatibility assumption identifies that composite with the output’s scalar homomorphism. Ordinary linear composition is the identity-homomorphism special case. Compared with [Schweigert Def.1.1.3/Lem.1.1.23](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L478).

Restricting scalars keeps the same function and reinterprets an S-linear map as R-linear. The modules already carry both scalar actions, with an assumption that every S-linear map respects the R-action. Usual restriction along a ring homomorphism supplies this compatibility; no injective inclusion of R into S is required. Compared with [Schweigert Lem.1.1.23](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L417).

Compatibility here means that every S-linear map between the specified modules also preserves the given R-actions. It is a property of those actions, not a new scalar action. R need not itself be a ring or semiring. Compatible scalar towers are one sufficient construction, rather than a requirement of the definition. Compared with [Schweigert Lem.1.1.23](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L345).

The identity linear map sends each element to itself and preserves addition and scalar multiplication. It works over a semiring, without a basis or finite-dimensionality assumption. In a zero module the identity equals the zero map; the declaration does not require the module or scalar semiring to be nontrivial. Compared with [Schweigert Def.1.1.3](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L260).

Multiplying first on the left by a and then on the right by b gives the linear map x↦(a·x)·b. The two stated compatibility conditions ensure that both multiplications respect scalars. Associativity is not assumed, so the displayed parentheses are essential; the construction does not replace this by a·(x·b). Compared with [Schweigert Def.1.1.3/Rem.1.1.4](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L1063).

Left multiplication by a is the map x↦a·x. It is linear when multiplication on the left commutes with the scalar action, so a·(r•x)=r•(a·x). Distributivity supplies additivity. No multiplicative identity, associativity, commutativity, or additive inverses in the multiplication structure are assumed. Compared with [Schweigert Def.1.1.3/Rem.1.1.4](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L1018).

Right multiplication by b is the map x↦x·b. Its scalar compatibility is (r•x)·b=r•(x·b), distinct from the condition used for left multiplication. Distributivity makes the map additive. The source allows nonassociative multiplication and does not require a multiplicative identity or commutativity. Compared with [Schweigert Def.1.1.3/Rem.1.1.4](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L1043).

A supplied two-sided inverse of a semilinear map is semilinear for the inverse scalar homomorphism. Both inverse identities are assumptions, and the scalar homomorphisms must also be inverse to each other. This construction packages the supplied function; it does not assign a default inverse to a noninvertible map. Compared with [Schweigert Def.1.1.3/Lem.1.1.23](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L554).

A semilinear map sends c•x to σ(c)•f(x), where σ is the specified homomorphism between the scalar semirings. Omitting σ would generally be wrong; ordinary linearity is the case σ=id. For complex conjugation, for example, the scalar is conjugated. Additive inverses and scalar fields are not required. Compared with [Schweigert Def.1.1.3/Lem.1.1.23](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L325).

Every additive homomorphism between abelian groups is automatically integer-linear. Positive integers act by repeated addition, negative integers by negating that sum, and zero acts by zero. This construction keeps the original function and uses those canonical actions; it does not require the groups to be torsion-free or finitely generated. Compared with [Schweigert Ex.1.1.9](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L709).

Every homomorphism of commutative additive monoids is automatically linear over the natural numbers. Multiplication by n means adding an element n times, with zero repetitions giving zero. The construction keeps the same function. Additive inverses, cancellation, and torsion-free behavior are unnecessary, so this also covers monoids that are not groups. Compared with [Wodzicki §2.3.4.20](https://math.berkeley.edu/~wodzicki/105.S12/Measure-20120305.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L691).

An abelian group becomes an integer module by repeated addition: positive n adds n copies, zero gives zero, and negative n gives the negative of the corresponding positive sum. These are the canonical integer actions, compatible with the original group operations. No torsion-free or divisibility assumption is imposed. Compared with [Schweigert Ex.1.1.9](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/NatInt.lean#L73).

A commutative additive monoid becomes a module over the natural-number semiring by repeated addition. Zero repetitions give the additive identity and one repetition leaves an element unchanged. Commutativity ensures distributivity over addition. Subtraction and cancellation are not assumed, and no multiplication between elements of the monoid is needed. Compared with [Wodzicki §2.3.4.20](https://math.berkeley.edu/~wodzicki/105.S12/Measure-20120305.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/NatInt.lean#L58).

A module over a ring already has additive inverses, even if its elements were initially presented only as a commutative additive monoid: define −x as (−1)•x. The module laws give (−1)•x+x=0. The construction retains addition and zero, and integer multiplication becomes multiplication by the corresponding integer cast. Compared with [Schweigert Rem.1.1.4(4)](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/NatInt.lean#L90).

Functions from any index set into a module form a module by adding and scaling values pointwise. The index set may be infinite; there is no finite-support or summability condition. If it is empty, there is exactly one function, giving the zero module. This instance uses the ordinary pointwise operations. Compared with [Schweigert Def.1.2.1](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Pi.lean#L52).

The product of an arbitrary family of modules over one semiring is a module with coordinatewise operations. The factors may differ, and elements need not have finite support. No finiteness assumption on the index set is required. For an empty family the product has one element, so it is the zero module. Compared with [Schweigert Def.1.2.1](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Pi.lean#L37).

Two semilinear maps from the scalar semiring itself agree everywhere if they agree at one, provided they use the same scalar homomorphism. Every input r equals r·1, so its image is σ(r)•f(1). This criterion concerns that particular source module; a value at one cannot determine an arbitrary module map. Compared with [Schweigert Ex.1.1.9(2)](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean#L456).

For nonnegative concentration κ, this weights uniform probability on the circle by exp(κ cos(θ−m))/I₀(κ). Probability Haar already includes the factor 1/(2π), explaining its absence from the density. Zero concentration gives the uniform law; negative concentration deliberately gives the zero measure. The denominator is positive, so division never uses Lean’s zero-denominator convention. See [Mardia–Sriram, equation (1.3), p.4](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/192132/12/s13171-022-00298-z.pdf) and [DLMF 10.32.1 and 10.32.3](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.32) and [the definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/VonMises/Basic.lean#L171). Native Checks pass: [normalization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/VonMises/Basic.lean#L194), [zero concentration](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/VonMises/Basic.lean#L227), [negative concentration](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/VonMises/Basic.lean#L183), and [Fourier moments](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/VonMises/Basic.lean#L250).
Probability precisely for nonnegative concentration.
Zero concentration gives probability Haar measure.
Negative concentration gives the declared zero measure.
Integer Fourier moments have the positive-exponential phase and I_|n|/I_0 normalization.

This reduces a centered real Cauchy variable modulo 2π and shifts it by the circle point m. The scale γ is nonnegative; γ=0 explicitly gives a point mass at m. Its Fourier moments use exp(+inθ), yielding exp(inm)exp(−γ|n|). Thus γ corresponds to the usual wrapped-Cauchy parameter ρ=exp(−γ), with no extra 2π factor. See [Mardia–Sriram, wrapping construction and equation (1.4), p.4](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/192132/12/s13171-022-00298-z.pdf) and [the definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/WrappedCauchy/Basic.lean#L70). Native Checks pass: [representative independence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/WrappedCauchy/Basic.lean#L86), [zero scale](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/WrappedCauchy/Basic.lean#L105), and [Fourier moments](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/WrappedCauchy/Basic.lean#L157).
A real representative gives the same quotient pushforward of the shifted Cauchy law.
Zero scale gives the point mass at the circle location.
Integer Fourier moments equal exp(i n m) exp(-gamma |n|).

For a jointly Gaussian vector with positive-semidefinite covariance S and positive-definite observed block S₂₂, the conditional mean is m₁+S₁₂S₂₂⁻¹(x₂−m₂) and covariance S₁₁−S₁₂S₂₂⁻¹S₂₁. Equality holds almost everywhere under the observed law, as conditional distributions require. The inverse is genuine; the joint covariance may be singular, and zero residual covariance gives a point mass. See [Muirhead, Theorem 1.2.11, pp.12–13](https://api.pageplace.de/preview/DT0400.9780470316702_A23667040/preview-9780470316702_A23667040.pdf) and [the conditional kernel](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Gaussian/Conditional.lean#L171). Native Checks pass: [the scalar Gaussian carrier](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Gaussian/LowDimension.lean#L74) , [the bivariate kernel calculation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Gaussian/LowDimension.lean#L206), and [the computed bivariate conditional family](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Gaussian/LowDimension.lean#L232); equal coordinates have correlation 1 and zero residual variance within that family.
The actual one-dimensional multivariate carrier equals the scalar Gaussian, including zero variance.
The native bivariate kernel has the explicit correlation mean and variance, including perfect correlation.
The computed bivariate kernel is the actual regular conditional distribution for positive observed variance.
